findings.title: Recovery codes in user storage are never marked as used, so they can be replayed
findings.body: isValid for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks that the submitted code is present in the stored JSON list. Nothing records that a code was consumed. The local-DB path tracks used codes via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode/allCodesUsed, so this is a behavioural gap. In the user-storage path, allCodesUsed() can never become true, so the authenticator never removes the credential or requires regeneration, and a recovery code can be used repeatedly. The same reasoning applies to the new getCredential lookup order in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils, which prefers federated credentials that never expire.

findings.title: Plaintext recovery codes are sent to external user storage
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...). Whenever the user storage accepts the type, the raw recovery codes are written to the external store, which is not under Keycloak's control. The local path hashes the codes (via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues). Storing raw single-use secrets in a federated backend is a credential-exposure risk and should be hashed or the user storage should be restricted.

findings.title: Serialization failure wrapped as a generic RuntimeException
findings.body: JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString throws IOException, which is rethrown as a bare RuntimeException with no message. Any failure surfaces as an unhelpful 500 during required-action processing. A more specific exception or message would make diagnosis easier.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() on credential lookup
findings.body: credentialModelOpt.get() is called without isPresent(). If the user has no recovery codes in either storage, this throws NoSuchElementException while rendering the login page. The old code had the same unchecked get(), but the new helper now returns Optional explicitly, so the caller should handle the empty case.

findings.title: Typo in authenticator config alias
findings.body: The config alias is set to "delayed-suthenticator-config", which is a misspelling of 'authenticator'. It is harmless to behaviour but is a copy-paste defect in test code that should be corrected for clarity.
